nonLabourLines.description: Legacy data migration tooling & Oracle export licensing

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is based on backlog point-sizing and typical throughput assumptions only.

Story points converted to effort using a rough baseline of ~6-7 hours/point for backend-heavy work, ~5-6 hours/point for frontend-heavy work, adjusted per task complexity (e.g. migration and RBAC weighted higher due to integration/testing risk).
1 sprint = 2 weeks; team capacity assumed at 1.5 FTE Backend (~120 hrs/sprint), 1.0 FTE Frontend (~80 hrs/sprint), 0.6 FTE QA (~48 hrs/sprint), 0.4 FTE DevOps (~32 hrs/sprint).

DevOps Engineer is staffed at only 0.4 FTE (~32 hrs/sprint); this is thin relative to the CI/staging setup (PW-1) and Stripe webhook/reconciliation infra (PW-7) it must support, so DevOps work is scoped tightly to setup and integration support only, with ongoing maintenance assumed to fall to Backend Developers.

QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE is assumed to focus testing effort on the Urgent/High priority items (auth, RBAC, payments, migration) with lighter coverage on Medium priority items (design system, invoice UI).

Legacy data migration (PW-8) assumed to require a dedicated data-validation and reconciliation pass; non-labour cost includes tooling/licensing for Oracle export, but does not include any target-system storage cost increases.
Payment provider integration (PW-7) assumes standard Stripe Checkout/Elements + webhooks; no custom PCI-scope card handling.
Design system (PW-2) assumes Angular component library scoped to the components explicitly listed (buttons, forms, tables, dialogs, theming) with no extensive Storybook/documentation site build-out.
Estimate assumes no significant scope changes or new backlog items are introduced mid-delivery.
Non-labour costs are limited to known direct tooling/infra/licensing costs; no allowance made for third-party consulting or extra cloud spend beyond initial staging setup.
input.reasoning: Effort was sized per backlog item using story points as a proxy for complexity, then allocated across the four staffed roles in proportion to the nature of each task (e.g., PW-8 migration is backend + QA heavy, PW-2 design system is frontend heavy, PW-1 is DevOps + Backend). Total allocated hours were checked against each role's FTE capacity over an assumed project duration of roughly 8-9 sprints (16-18 weeks) to confirm the allocation is plausible without overloading any role — DevOps in particular is capacity-constrained at 0.4 FTE and is flagged as a risk. Non-labour costs cover Stripe sandbox/testing, Oracle migration tooling/licensing, and initial staging infrastructure setup. The Most Likely scenario is set equal to the sum of line items (110,732 USD); Optimistic (~96,000) reflects faster-than-expected delivery with fewer QA/rework cycles, and Pessimistic (~130,000) reflects risk materializing in the highest-uncertainty items (legacy migration data quality issues, Stripe reconciliation edge cases, RBAC enforcement complexity across API and UI).

reductions.description: Descope Legacy Data Migration (PW-8) reconciliation/validation pass to a follow-on phase, delivering only core record migration now
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend and QA hours allocated to PW-8 by roughly 30%; validation and reconciliation work deferred to a post-launch phase.

reductions.description: Defer Design System (PW-2) theming tokens and advanced dialog/table components; ship with baseline component set only
reductions.effect: Cuts Frontend Developer hours on PW-2 by ~35%, reusing a lighter-weight component set for initial launch.

reductions.description: Reduce QA Engineer coverage on Medium-priority items (PW-2, PW-6) to smoke-testing only, keeping full regression coverage on Urgent/High items
reductions.effect: Lowers QA hours on Medium-priority backlog items; relies on developer self-testing for lower-risk UI work.

reductions.description: Delay initial staging infrastructure spend by using a shared/lower-tier environment until closer to first release
reductions.effect: Removes dedicated staging infra setup cost in favor of a shared lower-cost environment for the first 1-2 sprints.
